headline: High risk: shared filesystem and server-side flow execution make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx ingests filesystem and MCP/server artifacts, while Langflow can chain agents and wire tools into flows. That creates a plausible path where ctx outputs or files are fed into Langflow nodes as trusted content. The bridge is not proven automatic, so I rate it medium rather than high.
conditions: IF ctx outputs are copied into a Langflow prompt or node input without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF a Langflow flow reads ctx-generated files from the shared filesystem, attacker-controlled instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all ctx outputs before passing them into Langflow.
Disable automatic ingestion of ctx files into Langflow prompts.
Review any flow node that parses free-form text from ctx.
Use a separate workspace directory for each agent.
requires-engineering: add content filtering or schema validation between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers, and Langflow reads/writes the server filesystem while sending data to model providers and arbitrary HTTP services. If they share a workspace, ctx artifacts can be exposed to Langflow and then exfiltrated through Langflow's broad egress. The pairwise leakage path is credible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents mount the same directory, ctx logs or graph data can be read by Langflow.
IF a Langflow flow forwards those files to an external model provider or HTTP service, the data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces.
Restrict Langflow egress to approved endpoints only.
Move ctx logs and graph data out of any shared directory.
Rotate or redact secrets in any shared files before flow execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can install packages and use filesystem-backed MCP/Claude Code hooks, while Langflow can execute shell, install packages, and write the filesystem. Both can mutate the same local environment, and Langflow's server-side state is shared across instances. Without explicit locking or isolation, concurrent writes and package changes can collide and corrupt state.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory, concurrent writes can overwrite each other's files.
IF both agents install or update packages in the same environment, dependency state can diverge or break.
mitigations: Run each agent in its own virtual environment.
Use separate working directories and package caches.
Serialize package-install steps.
Avoid sharing mutable git or build state.
requires-engineering: add file locks or an orchestrator-level mutex.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code events and Langflow can chain multiple agents in graph-based flows. That makes it plausible for ctx output to become Langflow input without a verification gate, and for Langflow to act on it through downstream tools or model calls. Because the pair can automate multi-step workflows, a bad upstream assumption can cascade into repeated wrong actions.
conditions: IF a Langflow node consumes ctx-generated text as authoritative, errors can propagate downstream.
IF a flow uses ctx output to trigger shell or HTTP actions, the cascade can affect multiple steps.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action node.
Require structured outputs from ctx and validate them in Langflow.
Log and diff intermediate values between nodes.
Disable automatic action nodes for untrusted inputs.
requires-engineering: add verification or policy gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and intermediate outputs. If the same regulated data class is routed through both, their retention and storage behaviors may differ, creating a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not show a specific residency breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into both agents, their logging and storage policies must be aligned.
IF Langflow stores credentials or outputs longer than ctx retains logs, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared flows.
Document retention for ctx logs and Langflow stores.
Purge intermediate outputs after each run.
Store secrets only in Langflow's credential store, not in files.
requires-engineering: implement a unified retention and deletion policy.
